You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE Student (
    StuID INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    LName VARCHAR(12),
    Fname VARCHAR(12),
    Age INTEGER,
    Sex VARCHAR(1),
    Major INTEGER,
    Advisor INTEGER,
    city_code VARCHAR(3)
);

CREATE TABLE Has_Pet (
    StuID INTEGER,
    PetID INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (StuID) REFERENCES Student(StuID),
    FOREIGN KEY (PetID) REFERENCES Pets(PetID)
);

CREATE TABLE Pets (
    PetID INTEGER   PRIMARY KEY,
    PetType VARCHAR(20),
    pet_age INTEGER,
    weight REAL
);

What kind of “analysis” do you want (counts, breakdowns, correlations, lists)? Here are some common SQL analyses you can run on this schema—tell me which ones you need and any filters (e.g., by major, city_code, age range).

### 1) Basic student summary
```sql
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_students,
  AVG(Age) AS avg_age,
  MIN(Age) AS min_age,
  MAX(Age) AS max_age
FROM Student;
```

### 2) Students by major
```sql
SELECT Major, COUNT(*) AS num_students
FROM Student
GROUP BY Major
ORDER BY num_students DESC, Major;
```

### 3) Students by sex
```sql
SELECT Sex, COUNT(*) AS num_students
FROM Student
GROUP BY Sex
ORDER BY num_students DESC;
```

### 4) Students by city
```sql
SELECT city_code, COUNT(*) AS num_students
FROM Student
GROUP BY city_code
ORDER BY num_students DESC, city_code;
```

### 5) Age distribution (by exact age)
```sql
SELECT Age, COUNT(*) AS num_students
FROM Student
GROUP BY Age
ORDER BY Age;
```

### 6) Pet ownership rate (students with/without pets)
```sql
SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN hp.StuID IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS students_with_pets,
  SUM(CASE WHEN hp.StuID IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS students_without_pets
FROM Student s
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT StuID FROM Has_Pet) hp
  ON hp.StuID = s.StuID;
```

### 7) Pets by type (overall)
```sql
SELECT p.PetType, COUNT(*) AS num_pets
FROM Pets p
GROUP BY p.PetType
ORDER BY num_pets DESC, p.PetType;
```

### 8) Students by pet type (how many students own each type)
```sql
SELECT p.PetType, COUNT(DISTINCT hp.StuID) AS num_students
FROM Has_Pet hp
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
GROUP BY p.PetType
ORDER BY num_students DESC, p.PetType;
```

### 9) Average student age by pet ownership
```sql
SELECT
  CASE WHEN hp.StuID IS NULL THEN 'No Pet' ELSE 'Has Pet' END AS pet_status,
  AVG(s.Age) AS avg_age,
  COUNT(*) AS num_students
FROM Student s
LEFT JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT StuID FROM Has_Pet) hp
  ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
GROUP BY CASE WHEN hp.StuID IS NULL THEN 'No Pet' ELSE 'Has Pet' END;
```

Which output do you want, and do you want it grouped by **Major**, **city_code**, **Sex**, or filtered to a subset of students?
Only interested in students who have pets.

```sql
-- Students who have at least one pet (unique students)
SELECT DISTINCT
  s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname, s.Age, s.Sex, s.Major, s.Advisor, s.city_code
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
ORDER BY s.StuID;
```

If you want them *with pet details* (one row per pet):
```sql
SELECT
  s.StuID, s.LName, s.Fname,
  p.PetID, p.PetType, p.pet_age, p.weight
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
JOIN Pets p ON p.PetID = hp.PetID
ORDER BY s.StuID, p.PetID;
```
I want to see their first names and ages too.

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  s.Fname,
  s.Age
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
ORDER BY s.Fname, s.Age;
```

If you also want the student id (to avoid ambiguity when names repeat):
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  s.StuID,
  s.Fname,
  s.Age
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
ORDER BY s.StuID;
```
make sure to include ages of students too

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  s.Fname,
  s.Age
FROM Student s
JOIN Has_Pet hp ON hp.StuID = s.StuID
ORDER BY s.Fname, s.Age;
```
